newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL shares rise sharply on foreign fund buying.
newsitem.headline: KL shares rise sharply on foreign fund buying.

text.p: Malaysian shares rallied towards the close on Friday as foreign institutional funds selectively bought blue-chip stocks after sharp falls in recent weeks, dealers and analysts said.
At the close the benchmark Composite Index of 100 large-capitalised stocks gained 17.79 points to 1,097.96.
"We have been net buyers today. There has been an American and a Japanese buy programme in the market," said an institutional dealer at a local bank-backed brokerage house.
Volume rose slightly to 267 million shares valued at 1,609 ringgit. Gainers outpaced losers 359 to 233.
Power utility Tenaga closed 20 cents higher to 11.80 ringgit after the Malaysian government approved a long-awaited 8.3 percent increase in tariffs on Wednesday.

Financial services companies MBf Capital and Suria Capital were the two most active stocks. Rumours of a possible merger between the two, or a takeover by MBf Capital of Suria Capital resurfaced, boosting the prices and volumes of the stocks, analysts and dealers said.
MBf Capital rose 88 cents to 4.60 ringgit with 26.4 million shares traded, and Suria Capital gained 43 cents to 3.06 ringgit, with 19.4 million shares changing hands.
Officials at both companies were unavailable for comment.
"Some funds came over to Malaysia after some switching out of Manila, and on some bargain hunting," said an institutional dealer at Jupiter Securities.
"If the market is still good on Monday, we would be able to say we have passed the worst," the dealer said.

Analysts said the Kuala Lumpur market was still sensitive to movements on Wall Street. Friday's forthcoming U.S. jobs data would be watched closely for a possible indicator of the direction of share prices there, said analysts.

On the Kuala Lumpur Options and Financial Futures Exchange the spot May contract closed 5.7 points higher to 1,084.7 with 1,033 lots traded. The June futures contract rose 5.1 points to 1,088.0 with four lots changing hands.
